newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO must have at least one Baltic member - Lithuania.
newsitem.headline: NATO must have at least one Baltic member - Lithuania.

text.p: At least one of the three Baltic countries queuing to join NATO should be included in the first wave of the alliance's enlargement, Lithuanian Foreign Minister Algirdas Saudargas said on Wednesday.

"In order to make the (NATO) enlargement process a success, it is important that at least one Baltic country should be invited to join the alliance with the first group," Saudargas told a meeting of NATO ambassadors and aspirant members.
Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia have all applied for NATO membership, viewing its protective embrace as their only shield from a potentially hostile Russia.

Saudargas said inclusion of one Baltic state at this stage would send a positive signal to the region which seeks recognition for its move to democracy and free market reforms since quitting the former Soviet Union six years ago.
"Such a step would ensure that the policy of non-recognition has not been abandoned and that the destiny of the three Baltic states is not hostage to Cold War stereotypes," he said.

"We want to be part of the alliance because both common sense and the success of the alliance members suggest that the best, the most effective, and the least expensive way of building and developing a national defence system is through participation in collective defence arrangements.
"There is no other alternative to such arrangements but NATO," Saudargas said.
NATO members are set to decide on whom to invite into the first wave of its expansion at a summit in Madrid in July. Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are the favourites.
Analysts and diplomats have said the Baltic countries have little chance of making the first round because Moscow would view such a move as a direct provocation.
Moscow objects to NATO's enlargement plans and is particularly sensitive about the Baltics, the Soviet Union's western flank during the Cold War and home to large Russian minorities.
